title: Cripto-1 acts as a molecular bridge linking nodal to ALK4 via distinct structural domains.
authors: Chu, Kit-Yee; Crawford, Amberly N; Krah, Bradon S; Thamilselvan, Vijayalakshmi; Malik, Anjali; Aitas, Nina A; Martinez-Hackert, Erik
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Cripto-1介导Nodal与ALK4受体形成三元复合物的信号机制，虽用AlphaFold3建模和SPR分析蛋白互作，但对象为蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: The TGF-beta family ligand Nodal is an essential regulator of embryonic development, orchestrating key processes such as germ layer specification and body axis formation through activation of SMAD2/3-mediated signaling. Significantly, this activation requires the co-receptor Cripto-1. However, despite their essential roles in embryogenesis, the molecular mechanism through which Cripto-1 enables Nodal to activate the SMAD2/3 pathway has remained elusive. Intriguingly, Cripto-1 also has been shown to antagonize other TGF-beta family ligands, raising questions about its diverse functions. To clarify how Cripto-1 modulates TGF-beta signaling, we integrated AlphaFold3 modeling, surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based protein-protein interaction analysis, domain-specific anti-Cripto-1 antibodies, and functional studies in NTERA-2 cells. In contrast to canonical TGF-beta signaling, where ligands bridge type I and type II receptors for activation, Nodal, bound to the type II receptor, utilizes Cripto-1 to recruit the type I receptor ALK4, forming a unique ternary complex for SMAD2/3 activation. Our molecular characterization of Cripto-1-mediated Nodal signaling clarifies the unique role of this enigmatic co-receptor and advances our understanding of signaling regulation within the TGF-beta family. These insights have potential implications for both developmental biology and cancer research.
abstract_zh: TGF-beta家族配体Nodal是胚胎发育的重要调节因子，通过激活SMAD2/3介导的信号传导，协调胚层特化和体轴形成等关键过程。值得注意的是，这一激活过程需要共受体Cripto-1的参与。然而，尽管它们在胚胎发生中具有重要作用，Cripto-1使Nodal激活SMAD2/3通路的分子机制至今仍不明确。有趣的是，Cripto-1也被证明能拮抗其他TGF-beta家族配体，这引发了对其多种功能的疑问。为阐明Cripto-1如何调节TGF-beta信号传导，我们整合了AlphaFold3建模、基于表面等离子共振（SPR）的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析、结构域特异性抗Cripto-1抗体以及NTERA-2细胞中的功能研究。与经典TGF-beta信号传导中配体桥接I型和II型受体以激活的方式不同，与II型受体结合的Nodal利用Cripto-1招募I型受体ALK4，形成独特的SMAD2/3激活三元复合物。我们对Cripto-1介导的Nodal信号传导的分子表征阐明了这一神秘共受体的独特作用，并推进了我们对TGF-beta家族信号传导调控的理解。这些见解对发育生物学和癌症研究均具有潜在意义。
